chunks.st: except for a deaf-mute,

chunks.en: a shoteh, a child, a blind person, or a non-Jew.
chunks.st: an imbecile, or a minor, or a blind person, or a gentile.

mishnayos.summary: A messenger must be able to understand both when he gets the get and when he hands it over. If he was not able at the start, he cannot bring it.

chunks.en: If a child received the get and then grew up,
chunks.st: If a minor received the bill of divorce and then reached the age of majority,

chunks.en: or a cheresh who then could hear,
chunks.st: or one received it when he was a deaf-mute and then became able to hear,

chunks.en: or a blind man who then could see,
chunks.st: or one received it when he was blind and then became able to see,

chunks.en: or a shoteh who then became clear-minded,
chunks.st: or one received it when he was an imbecile and then became halakhically competent,

chunks.en: or a non-Jew who then became a Jew,
chunks.st: or one received it when he was a gentile and then converted,

words.note: A ger is someone who became Jewish.

chunks.he: פָּסוּל. אֲבָל פִּקֵּחַ וְנִתְחָרֵשׁ וְחָזַר וְנִתְפַּקֵּחַ,
chunks.en: he is not fit. But one who could hear, then became a cheresh, then could hear again,
chunks.st: in all of these cases he is unfit to bring the bill of divorce. However, if one received it when he was able to hear, and then became a deaf-mute, and then again became able to hear;

chunks.en: or could see, became blind, and then could see again,
chunks.st: or if one received it when he was able to see, and then became blind, and then again became able to see;

chunks.en: or was clear-minded, became a shoteh, and then became clear-minded again,
chunks.st: or one received it when he was halakhically competent, and then became an imbecile, and then again became halakhically competent,

chunks.en: he is fit. This is the rule:
chunks.st: in all of these cases he is fit to bring the bill of divorce. This is the principle:

chunks.en: anyone who understands at the start and at the end is fit.
chunks.st: Anyone who is halakhically competent in the beginning and in the end is fit, even if there was time in the interim when he was unfit.

mishnayos.summary: Some women may not tell us that a woman's husband died, but they may bring her get, because the written get proves it. A woman may even bring her own get.

chunks.en: Even the women who are not believed
chunks.st: Even the women who are not deemed credible to

chunks.en: to say that her husband died,
chunks.st: testify on behalf of a woman and say: Her husband died,

chunks.en: are believed to bring her get:
chunks.st: and she is permitted to remarry, are deemed credible to bring her bill of divorce.

chunks.en: her mother-in-law, her mother-in-law's daughter, and her husband's other wife,
chunks.st: The relatives of the woman who are not deemed credible to testify that her husband has died are: Her mother-in-law; and her mother-in-law’s daughter; and her rival wife, i.e., another wife of her husband’s;

words.note: Long ago a man could have two wives, and each one is the other's tzarah.

chunks.en: and her brother-in-law's wife, and her husband's daughter.
chunks.st: and her yevama, i.e., her husband’s brother’s wife; and her husband’s daughter.

chunks.en: What is the difference between a get and death?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: What is the difference between a bill of divorce and death,
chunks.stMore: that certain women are deemed credible to testify about one but not the other?

chunks.en: That the writing proves it.
chunks.st: With regard to a bill of divorce, it is so that the writing proves
chunks.stMore: that the husband is divorcing his wife, and the testimony is needed only to supplement the bill of divorce.

chunks.en: The woman herself may bring her own get,
chunks.st: Similarly, the woman herself may bring her own bill of divorce,

chunks.en: as long as she says,
chunks.st: provided that she is required by the court to state in its presence:

chunks.en: "It was written in front of me, and it was signed in front of me."
chunks.st: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence, as the Gemara will explain.

mishnayos.stIntro: There are instances in which a woman’s testimony that another woman’s husband has died is not deemed credible (Yevamot 117a). If there is a presumption that due to their familial relationship the two women hate each other, there is concern that the woman is testifying falsely in order to harm the other woman. By doing so, she can cause the other woman to remarry. If her original husband then proves to be living, she will be required to leave her second husband. This mishna teaches:

mishnayos.summary: A get must be written for one special woman. The mishnah gives examples of a get that was not written for her, which may not be used.

chunks.he: כָּל גֵּט שֶׁנִּכְתַּב שֶׁלֹּא לְשׁוּם אִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: Any get that was not written for a certain woman
chunks.st: Any bill of divorce that was not written for the sake of a specific woman

chunks.en: is not valid. How so?
chunks.st: is invalid. How so?

chunks.en: A man was walking through the market and heard
chunks.st: In a case of a man who was passing through the marketplace and heard the sound of scribes

chunks.en: the voice of scribes reading out to their students,
chunks.st: who write bills of divorce dictating the text to their students:

chunks.en: "The man so-and-so is divorcing
chunks.st: The man so-and-so divorces

chunks.en: so-and-so, from such-and-such a place,"
chunks.st: so-and-so from the place of such and such;

chunks.he: וְאָמַר, זֶה שְּׁמִי וְזֶה שֵּׁם אִשְׁתִּי,
chunks.en: and he said, "That is my name, and that is my wife's name,"
chunks.st: and the man said: This is my name and that is the name of my wife,

chunks.en: it is not fit to divorce with it.
chunks.st: and he wishes to use this bill for his divorce, this bill is unfit for him to divorce his wife with it,
chunks.stMore: as it was not written for the sake of any woman.

chunks.en: Even more than that:
chunks.st: Moreover,

chunks.he: כָּתַב לְגָרֵשׁ בּוֹ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְנִמְלַךְ,
chunks.en: if he wrote it to divorce his wife and then changed his mind,
chunks.st: if one wrote a bill of divorce with which to divorce his wife but later reconsidered,

chunks.en: and a man from his town found him and said to him,
chunks.st: and a resident of his town found him and said to him:

chunks.he: שְׁמִי כִשְׁמֶךָ וְשֵׁם אִשְׁתִּי כְשֵׁם אִשְׁתֶּךָ,
chunks.en: "My name is like your name, and my wife's name is like your wife's name,"
chunks.st: My name is the same as your name, and my wife’s name is the same as your wife’s name,

chunks.en: it is not fit to divorce with it.
chunks.st: and we reside in the same town; give me the bill of divorce and I will use it; the bill of divorce is unfit for the second man to divorce his wife with it.

chunks.en: Even more than that:
chunks.st: Moreover,

chunks.he: הָיוּ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים וּשְׁמוֹתֵיהֶן שָׁווֹת,
chunks.en: if he had two wives, and their names were the same,
chunks.st: if one had two wives and their names were identical,

chunks.en: and he wrote it to divorce the older one,
chunks.st: and he wrote a bill of divorce to divorce the older one

chunks.en: he may not divorce the younger one with it.
chunks.st: and then reconsidered, he may not divorce the younger one with it.

chunks.en: Even more than that:
chunks.st: Moreover,

chunks.en: if he said to the scribe,
chunks.st: if he said to the scribe:

chunks.en: "Write it, and I will divorce whichever one I want,"
chunks.st: Write a bill of divorce for whichever one of them that I will want and I will divorce her with it,

chunks.en: it is not fit to divorce with it.
chunks.st: this bill of divorce is unfit for him to divorce either wife with it.

mishnayos.summary: A scribe may prepare the main part of documents ahead of time, leaving empty spaces for names and dates. But for a get, Rabbi Elazar says it must all be written for her.

chunks.en: Someone who writes the main form of gittin ahead of time
chunks.st: With regard to a scribe who writes the standard part [tofes] of bills of divorce
chunks.stMore: in advance, so that when one requests a bill of divorce, he will need to add only the details unique to this case,

chunks.en: must leave empty the place for the man's name,
chunks.st: he must leave empty the place in the bill of divorce for the name of the man,

chunks.en: and the place for the woman's name, and the place for the date.
chunks.st: and the place for the name of the woman, and the place for the date.

chunks.en: For loan documents,
chunks.st: If a scribe writes the standard part of loan documents,

chunks.en: he must leave empty the place for the lender,
chunks.st: he must leave empty the place of the name of the lender,

chunks.en: the place for the borrower,
chunks.st: the place of the name of the borrower,

chunks.en: the place for the money, and the place for the date.
chunks.st: the place of the amount of the money being loaned, and the place of the date.

chunks.en: For documents of a sale,
chunks.st: If the scribe writes the standard part of documents of sale of land,

chunks.he: צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּנִּיחַ מְקוֹם הַלּוֹקֵחַ וּמְקוֹם הַמּוֹכֵר
chunks.en: he must leave empty the place for the buyer and the place for the seller,
chunks.st: he must leave empty the place for the name of the purchaser, and the place for the name of the seller,

chunks.he: וּמְקוֹם הַמָּעוֹת וּמְקוֹם הַשָּׂדֶה וּמְקוֹם הַזְּמַן,
chunks.en: and the place for the money, the place for the field, and the place for the date,
chunks.st: the place for the amount of the money for which the land is being purchased, the place for the description of the field that is being purchased, and the place of the date when the sale occurs.

chunks.en: because of a rule the Rabbis made.
chunks.st: This is necessary due to the ordinance,
chunks.stMore: as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says all of them are not valid.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda invalidates all of these documents if their standard parts were written in advance.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says all of them are valid,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar deems all of them valid

chunks.en: except for gittin of women,
chunks.st: except for bills of divorce,

chunks.en: as it says, "And he shall write for her," which means for her sake.
chunks.st: as it is stated in the Torah: “And he writes for her” (Deuteronomy 24:1), indicating that he must write the bill of divorce for her sake.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, one may not write even the standard part of the bill of divorce in advance, as that would not qualify as writing the bill of divorce for her sake.

mishnayos.summary: If a messenger lost a get and found it, it depends whether he can be sure it is the same one. We also assume a person is still alive, even if he is old, sick, or far away.

chunks.en: Someone who brings a get and it got lost from him,
chunks.st: With regard to an agent who brings a bill of divorce and it was lost from him,

chunks.en: if he found it right away,
chunks.st: if he finds it immediately

chunks.en: it is valid. But if not,
chunks.st: then the bill of divorce is valid. But if not,

chunks.en: it is not valid. If he found it in his bag or in his box,
chunks.explain: Maybe it is a different get with the same names.
chunks.st: then it is invalid,
chunks.stMore: as it is possible that the bill of divorce that he found is not the same one that he lost, and this second bill of divorce belongs to someone else whose name and wife’s name are identical to the names of the husband and wife in the lost bill of divorce. However, if

chunks.en: or if he recognizes it,
chunks.st: he found it in a ḥafisa or in a deluskema that he knows is his, or if he recognizes the actual bill of divorce,

chunks.he: כָּשֵׁר. הַמֵּבִיא גֵט וְהִנִּיחוֹ זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה,
chunks.en: it is valid. If someone brings a get and left the husband old or sick,
chunks.st: then it is valid. In the case of an agent who brings a bill of divorce to a woman, and when he had left the husband was elderly or sick,

chunks.en: he gives it to her, and we assume the husband is still alive.
chunks.st: the agent gives her the bill of divorce based on the presumption that the husband is still alive,
chunks.stMore: and there is no concern that in the meantime he has died, thereby canceling the bill of divorce.

chunks.en: The daughter of a Yisrael who is married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: Similarly, with regard to an Israelite woman who is married to a priest
chunks.stMore: and may therefore partake of teruma,

chunks.en: and her husband went overseas,
chunks.st: and her husband went to a country overseas,

chunks.en: may eat terumah, as we assume he is still alive.
chunks.st: she may continue to partake of teruma based on the presumption that her husband is still alive.

chunks.en: Someone who sends his chatas korban from overseas,
chunks.st: Similarly, in the case of one who sends his sin-offering from a country overseas,

words.note: A korban brought for a mistake.

chunks.en: they offer it, as we assume he is still alive.
chunks.st: the priests may offer it on the altar based on the presumption that the one who sent it is still alive.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Perata taught when we assume people in danger are still alive, and when we must be strict both ways, as if they might be alive or not.

chunks.he: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן
chunks.en: Three things Rabbi Elazar ben
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben

chunks.he: פַּרְטָא לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים וְקִיְּמוּ אֶת דְּבָרָיו.
chunks.en: Perata said before the Sages, and they agreed with his words.
chunks.st: Perata said three statements before the Sages as testimony from previous generations, and they upheld his statements:

chunks.en: About a city that an enemy army surrounded,
chunks.st: He spoke concerning the residents of a town that was surrounded by a camp of besiegers [karkom];

chunks.en: and about a ship being tossed in the sea,
chunks.st: and concerning the travelers in a ship that is cast about in the sea;

chunks.en: and about one who goes out to be judged,
chunks.st: and concerning one who is going out to be judged in a capital case;

chunks.en: that we assume they are alive.
chunks.st: that they are all presumed to be alive.

chunks.en: But a city that an enemy army captured,
chunks.st: However, concerning the residents of a town that was conquered by a camp of besiegers;

chunks.en: and a ship that was lost at sea,
chunks.st: and the travelers on a ship that was lost at sea;

chunks.en: and one who is taken out to be put to death,
chunks.st: and one who is going out to be executed after receiving his verdict;

chunks.he: נוֹתְנִין עֲלֵיהֶן חֻמְרֵי חַיִּים וְחֻמְרֵי מֵתִים,
chunks.en: we treat them strictly both as living and as dead.
chunks.st: in these cases one applies to them the stringencies of the living and the stringencies of the dead.
chunks.stMore: How so?

chunks.en: So a Yisrael's daughter married to a Kohen,
chunks.st: An Israelite woman married to a priest in one of these situations

chunks.en: or a Kohen's daughter married to a Yisrael,
chunks.st: or a daughter of a priest married to an Israelite in one of these situations

chunks.en: may not eat terumah.
chunks.explain: One may eat only if he is alive, the other only if he died.
chunks.st: may not partake of teruma. The first woman may not do so because she may partake of teruma only while her husband is alive, and the second may not do so because she may partake of teruma only if he has died.

mishnayos.summary: In Eretz Yisrael, a sick messenger may send the get with someone else, unless the husband also asked him to bring something back for him.

chunks.en: Someone who brings a get in Eretz Yisrael and became sick,
chunks.st: With regard to an agent who brings a bill of divorce in Eretz Yisrael, where his only responsibility is to transmit the bill of divorce to the wife, and the agent became sick,

chunks.en: may send it with someone else.
chunks.st: this agent may send it in the possession of another agent.

chunks.en: But if the husband said to him, "Take
chunks.st: But if the husband said to the agent: When you transmit the bill of divorce to my wife, take

chunks.en: such-and-such a thing from her for me,"
chunks.st: for me such and such an item from her that I left with her as a deposit, then

chunks.en: he may not send it with someone else,
chunks.st: he may not send it in the possession of another agent.

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁיְּהֵא פִקְדוֹנוֹ בְיַד אַחֵר:
chunks.en: because the husband does not want his things to be with someone else.
chunks.st: This is because it is assumed that it is not the desire of the husband that his deposit be in the possession of another person whom he did not appoint as his agent.

mishnayos.summary: A sick messenger from overseas can send the get with a new messenger through a beis din. The new messenger only says he was sent by the beis din.

chunks.en: Someone who brings a get from overseas and became sick,
chunks.st: With regard to an agent who is bringing a bill of divorce from a country overseas, who must attest to the fact that he witnessed the writing and signing of the bill of divorce, and he became sick and cannot complete his agency,

chunks.en: makes a beis din and sends it,
chunks.st: he appoints another agent in court and sends him.

words.note: A beis din is a Jewish court.

chunks.en: and says in front of them,
chunks.st: And the first agent says before the court:

chunks.en: "It was written in front of me and it was signed in front of me."
chunks.st: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence,
chunks.stMore: and on the basis of this the court deems the bill of divorce to be valid.

chunks.en: And the last messenger does not need to say,
chunks.st: And the final agent does not need to say:

chunks.en: "It was written in front of me and signed in front of me,"
chunks.st: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence.

chunks.en: rather he says,
chunks.st: Rather, it is sufficient that he says:

chunks.en: "I am a messenger of the beis din."
chunks.st: I am an agent of the court.

mishnayos.summary: A person may lend money to a Kohen, Levi, or poor person, and later pay himself back with their gifts. We assume they are still alive, but if they died he needs the heirs to agree.

chunks.he: הַמַּלְוֶה מָעוֹת אֶת הַכֹּהֵן וְאֶת הַלֵּוִי
chunks.en: Someone who lends money to a Kohen, to a Levi,
chunks.st: The mishna continues the discussion of the presumption that a person remains alive. With regard to one who lends money to a priest, or to a Levite,

chunks.he: וְאֶת הֶעָנִי לִהְיוֹת מַפְרִישׁ עֲלֵיהֶן מֵחֶלְקָן,
chunks.en: or to a poor person, so he can set aside their share for them,
chunks.st: or to a poor person, with the understanding that he will separate their portion of the teruma and tithes from his produce on the basis of that money,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he will subtract from the debt owed by the priest or Levite the value of the teruma and tithes separated from the produce,

chunks.en: sets it aside for them, as we assume they are still alive,
chunks.st: he may separate the teruma and tithes from his produce on the basis of that money with the presumption that they are still alive,

chunks.en: and he does not worry that maybe the Kohen died,
chunks.st: and he need not be concerned that perhaps the priest

chunks.en: or the Levi, or the poor person became rich.
chunks.st: or the Levite died in the interim, or that the poor person became rich
chunks.stMore: and is no longer eligible to be given the poor man’s tithe. The priest or Levite benefits from this arrangement, as he receives his gifts up front in the form of a loan. The Israelite benefits in that he does not need to seek out a priest or Levite each time he has produce from which he must separate teruma and tithes.

chunks.he: מֵתוּ, צָרִיךְ לִטֹּל רְשׁוּת מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין.
chunks.en: If they died, he must get permission from the heirs.
chunks.st: If in fact they died, then he must obtain permission from the heirs in order to continue the arrangement.

chunks.en: If he lent them money in front of a beis din,
chunks.st: However, if he lent money to the deceased, and he stipulated in the presence of the court
chunks.stMore: that the debt would be repaid in this manner, then

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לִטֹּל רְשׁוּת מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁים:
chunks.en: he does not need to get permission from the heirs.
chunks.st: he does not need to obtain permission from the heirs.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who set aside fruit or money to use for terumah and maaser may assume it is still there. Rabbi Yehuda says to check wine at three times of year in case it turned sour.

chunks.en: Someone who sets aside fruit so he can take off
chunks.st: With regard to one who sets aside produce with the understanding that he will separate

chunks.en: terumah and maaser with them,
chunks.st: terumot and tithes with it,
chunks.stMore: so that when he has untithed produce he can render it fit by declaring that the teruma and tithes that must be separated will be from the produce that he had set aside for this purpose,

words.note: A tenth of the crops, given to the Levi and others.

chunks.he: מָעוֹת לִהְיוֹת מַפְרִישׁ עֲלֵיהֶן מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
chunks.en: or money so he can use it for maaser sheni,
chunks.st: or one who sets aside money with the understanding that he will separate and to redeem second tithe with it,

words.note: Maaser sheni is eaten in Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: may set them aside, as we assume they are still there.
chunks.st: then he may later separate the teruma or tithe with them, based on the presumption that the produce or the money are extant.
chunks.stMore: He need not be concerned that perhaps the produce or money was lost in the meantime.

chunks.en: If they were lost,
chunks.st: If he discovers that they were lost,

chunks.en: he must worry from the same time the day before,
chunks.explain: He worries that they were lost in the past full day.
chunks.st: then he must be concerned that the produce or money that he set aside was lost, from the time until the same time, as will be explained in the Gemara,
chunks.stMore: and he must separate teruma and tithes from the produce a second time;

chunks.en: so says Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Elazar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: at three times we check the wine,
chunks.explain: To see if it turned into vinegar.
chunks.st: One checks the wine that is set aside to be used for separating terumot and tithes for other wine to see if it has turned to vinegar, which would render it unfit for this purpose, at three times during the year:

chunks.en: when the east wind blows after Sukkos,
chunks.st: When the east wind blows at the conclusion of the festival of Sukkot,

chunks.en: and when the grape buds come out,
chunks.st: and when the blossoms fall and the grape buds emerge and appear as small clusters,

chunks.en: and at the time water goes into the unripe grapes.
chunks.st: and at the time when water enters and fills the unripe grape. Since there is a change in the weather at these times, one should check to ensure that the wine has not turned to vinegar.

mishnayos.summary: A husband who sent a get may cancel it before it reaches his wife. Once she has it in her hand, he can no longer cancel it.

chunks.en: Someone who sends a get to his wife, and he caught up with the messenger,
chunks.st: In the case of one who sends a bill of divorce to his wife with an agent, and he reached the agent,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁלַח אַחֲרָיו שָׁלִיחַ וְאָמַר לוֹ,
chunks.en: or he sent another messenger after him and said to him,
chunks.st: or where he sent another agent after him, and he said to the agent delivering the bill of divorce:

chunks.en: "The get that I gave you is cancelled,"
chunks.st: The bill of divorce that I gave you, it is void,

chunks.en: then it is cancelled.
chunks.st: then this bill of divorce is hereby void.

chunks.en: If he got to his wife first, or he sent
chunks.st: Similarly, if the husband reached his wife before the bill of divorce reached her, or in a case where he sent

chunks.en: a messenger to her and said to her,
chunks.st: an agent to her, and he said, or had the agent say, to his wife:

chunks.en: "The get that I sent you is cancelled,"
chunks.st: The bill of divorce that I sent to you, it is void,

chunks.en: then it is cancelled.
chunks.st: then this bill of divorce is hereby void.

chunks.en: But once the get has reached her hand,
chunks.st: However, if he stated this once the bill of divorce had entered her possession,

chunks.en: he can no longer cancel it.
chunks.st: he can no longer render it void, as the divorce had already taken effect.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel the Elder made two rules to help the world: a husband may not cancel a get secretly in another beis din, and a get must include all the names the husband and wife are known by.

chunks.en: At first, a husband would make a beis
chunks.st: The mishna relates that initially, a husband who wished to render the bill of divorce void would convene a court

chunks.en: din in another place and cancel the get there.
chunks.st: elsewhere and render the bill of divorce void in the presence of the court before it reached his wife.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted an ordinance

chunks.en: that they should not do this,
chunks.st: that one should not do this,

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world.
chunks.stMore: The Gemara will explain what this means.

chunks.en: At first, he would change his name and her name,
chunks.st: Initially, the husband would change his name and her name,
chunks.stMore: from the names by which they were known where they formerly lived to the names by which they were known where the bill of divorce was written, and write

chunks.en: and the name of his city and the name of her city.
chunks.st: the name of his city and the name of her city.
chunks.stMore: One was not required to list all of the names by which the husband and the wife were known, but only the names in the place where the bill of divorce was being written.

chunks.he: וְהִתְקִין רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן שֶׁיְּהֵא כוֹתֵב,
chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule that the scribe should write,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted that the scribe should write in the bill of divorce:

chunks.he: אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי וְכָל שֵׁם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ,
chunks.en: "The man so-and-so, and every name he has,"
chunks.st: The man so-and-so, and any other name that he has,

chunks.he: אִשָּׁה פְלוֹנִית וְכָל שׁוּם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ,
chunks.en: "The woman so-and-so, and every name she has,"
chunks.st: and: The woman so-and-so, and any other name that she has.

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: The reason for this ordinance was for the betterment of the world,
chunks.stMore: as perhaps the people of a different city would not recognize the name written in the bill of divorce, and would claim that this bill of divorce does not belong to her.

mishnayos.summary: A widow must swear before collecting her kesubah from orphans. Rabban Gamliel let her make a promise instead. The mishnah lists more rules made to help the world, like Hillel's pruzbul.

chunks.en: A widow may not collect from the property
chunks.st: A widow can collect payment of her marriage contract from the property of orphans

chunks.en: of orphans unless she swears.
chunks.st: only by means of an oath
chunks.stMore: that she did not receive any part of the payment of the marriage contract during her husband’s lifetime. The mishna relates:

chunks.en: The courts stopped making her swear,
chunks.st: The courts refrained from administering an oath to her,
chunks.stMore: leaving the widow unable to collect payment of her marriage contract.

chunks.en: so Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule that she should
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel the Elder instituted that she should take, for

chunks.en: make any promise to the orphans that they want,
chunks.st: the benefit of the orphans, any vow that the orphans wished to administer to her,
chunks.stMore: e.g., that all produce will become prohibited to her if she received any payment of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: and then she collects her kesubah.
chunks.st: and after stating this vow, she collects payment of her marriage contract.
chunks.stMore: The mishna lists additional ordinances that were instituted for the betterment of the world:

words.note: The kesubah promises money to a wife if the marriage ends.

chunks.en: The witnesses sign on the get,
chunks.st: The witnesses sign their names on the bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: even though the bill of divorce is valid without their signatures,

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world,
chunks.stMore: as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.he: הִלֵּל הִתְקִין פְּרוֹזְבּוּל מִפְּנֵּי תִקּוּן הָעוֹלָם:
chunks.en: Hillel made the pruzbul to make the world better.
chunks.explain: A pruzbul lets a lender collect his loan even after Shemitah.
chunks.st: And Hillel instituted a document that prevents the Sabbatical Year from abrogating an outstanding debt [prosbol] for the betterment of the world, as the Gemara will explain.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what happens to a slave who was redeemed from captors, and to a slave who was promised to pay a debt and then set free.

chunks.en: A slave who was captured, and someone redeemed him,
chunks.st: In the case of a Canaanite slave that was captured, and Jews who had not owned him redeemed him,

chunks.en: if it was to be a slave,
chunks.st: if he was redeemed to be a slave

chunks.en: he stays a slave. If it was to be free,
chunks.st: then he will be a slave. If he was redeemed to be a freeman

chunks.en: he does not stay a slave.
chunks.st: then he will not be a slave.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: either way, he stays a slave.
chunks.st: Both in this case and in that case he will be a slave.

chunks.he: עֶבֶד שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ רַבּוֹ אַפּוֹתִיקִי לַאֲחֵרִים וְשִׁחְרְרוֹ,
chunks.en: A slave whose master promised him to others to pay a debt, and then set him free:
chunks.st: In the case of a slave whose master set him aside as designated repayment [apoteiki] of a debt to other people from whom he borrowed money, and afterward he emancipated him,

chunks.en: by the strict law,
chunks.st: then according to the letter of the law

chunks.en: the slave does not owe anything.
chunks.st: the slave bears no responsibility for the debt.

chunks.en: But to make the world better,
chunks.st: However, for the betterment of the world,

chunks.en: we force his master to make
chunks.st: his master is forced to make

chunks.en: him a free man,
chunks.st: him a freeman, and

chunks.en: and the slave writes a note promising to pay his value.
chunks.st: the slave writes a promissory note for his value to pay the debt to the creditor.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: the slave does not write anything, but the master just frees him.
chunks.st: He does not write a promissory note; he only emancipates the slave.

mishnayos.summary: A slave who is half free cannot marry anyone. Beis Shammai taught that his master must free him, and Beis Hillel agreed with them in the end.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶן חוֹרִין,
chunks.en: Someone who is half a slave and half free,
chunks.st: In the case of one who is a half-slave half-freeman because only one of his two owners emancipated him,

chunks.en: works for his master one day
chunks.st: he serves his master one day and

chunks.en: and for himself one day.
chunks.st: serves himself one day;

chunks.en: These are the words of Beis Hillel.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Beit Hillel.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: "You fixed things for his master,
chunks.st: Through such an arrangement you have remedied his master,
chunks.stMore: as his master loses nothing through this. However,

chunks.en: but you did not fix things for himself.
chunks.st: you have not remedied the slave himself,
chunks.stMore: as the slave himself remains in an unsustainable situation.

chunks.en: He cannot marry a maidservant,
chunks.st: It is not possible for him to marry a maidservant

chunks.en: since he is already half free.
chunks.st: because he is already a half-freeman,
chunks.stMore: as it is prohibited for a freeman to marry a maidservant.

chunks.en: He cannot marry a free woman,
chunks.st: It is also not possible for him to marry a free woman,

chunks.en: since he is still half a slave.
chunks.st: as he is still a half-slave.

chunks.en: Should he not marry at all? But the world was created
chunks.st: If you say he should be idle and not marry, but isn’t it true that the world was created

chunks.en: only for having children,
chunks.st: only for procreation,

chunks.en: as it says: He did not create it to be empty,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “He did not create it to be a waste;

chunks.en: He formed it to be lived in.
chunks.st: He formed it to be inhabited” (Isaiah 45:18)?

chunks.en: Rather, to make the world better,
chunks.st: Rather, for the betterment of the world

chunks.en: we force his master to make
chunks.st: his master is forced to make

chunks.en: him a free man,
chunks.st: him a freeman, and

chunks.en: and the slave writes a note promising to pay half his value."
chunks.st: the slave writes a promissory note accepting his responsibility to pay half his value to his master.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel changed their minds to teach
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel ultimately retracted their opinion,

chunks.en: like the words of Beis Shammai.
chunks.st: to rule in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai, that a half-slave must be set free.

mishnayos.summary: A slave sold to a non-Jew goes free. To help the world, we do not pay too much to free captives, help them escape, or buy back holy things for too much money.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ לְגוֹי אוֹ לְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: Someone who sells his slave to a non-Jew or to someone outside Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: In a case of one who sells his slave to gen-tiles, or even to a Jew outside of Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: the slave goes out free.
chunks.st: the slave is emancipated.
chunks.stMore: Since the slave, who is partially obligated in the fulfillment of mitzvot, would be restricted in his ability to fulfill them in his new situation, either because he would be under the authority of a gentile or because he will no longer be in Eretz Yisrael, the Sages penalized his original owner that he should become a freeman, so that if he succeeds in escaping his new owner, he is a full-fledged freeman.

chunks.en: We do not redeem captives
chunks.st: The captives are not redeemed

chunks.en: for more than they are worth,
chunks.st: for more than their actual monetary value,

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world;

chunks.en: And we do not help captives run away,
chunks.st: and one may not aid the captives in their attempt to escape from their captors

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world,
chunks.stMore: so that kidnappers will not be more restrictive with their captives to prevent them from escaping.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: it is to help the other captives.
chunks.explain: So the captors will not be cruel to the ones left behind.
chunks.st: For the betterment of the captives,
chunks.stMore: so that kidnappers will not avenge the escape of the captives by treating other captives with cruelty.

chunks.en: And we do not buy sifrei Torah,
chunks.st: And Torah scrolls,

chunks.en: tefillin, and mezuzos from non-Jews
chunks.st: phylacteries, or mezuzot are not purchased from the gentiles
chunks.stMore: when they acquire these objects, if they request

chunks.en: for more than they are worth,
chunks.st: more than their actual monetary value,

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world, so as not to cause an increase in the theft of sacred Jewish ritual objects in order to sell them for large sums of money.

mishnayos.summary: If a man divorced his wife because of a bad name or because of a neder, he may not marry her again. The Rabbis argue about which nedarim this applies to.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שֵׁם רָע,
chunks.en: Someone who sends away his wife because of a bad name,
may not take her back.
Because of a neder,

words.note: A neder is a promise that makes something forbidden.

chunks.en: he may not take her back.
Rabbi Yehuda says,
any neder that many people knew about,
he may not take her back.
But one that many people did not know about,
he may take her back. Rabbi Meir says,
any neder that needs a Sage to look into it,
he may not take her back.
But one that does not need a Sage to look into it,
he may take her back. Rabbi Eliezer said,

chunks.he: לֹא אָסְרוּ זֶה אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי זֶה.
chunks.en: they forbade this one only because of that one.
Rabbi Yosei the son of Rabbi Yehuda said,
once in Tzaidan, a man said to his wife,
"Konam, if I do not divorce you!"
chunks.explain: Konam is a word for a neder.

chunks.en: and he divorced her. And the Sages let him take her back,
to make the world better.

mishnayos.summary: If a man divorced his wife because he thought she could never have children, may he marry her again? And what if she later had children with someone else?

chunks.en: Someone who sends away his wife because she cannot have children,

words.note: A woman who cannot have children.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
he may not take her back.
And the Sages say,

chunks.he: יַחֲזִיר. נִשֵּׂאת לְאַחֵר וְהָיוּ לָהּ בָּנִים הֵימֶנּוּ,
chunks.en: he may take her back. If she married someone else and had children with him,
and she asks for her kesubah money,
Rabbi Yehuda said,
he may say to her,
"Your quiet is better for you than your speaking."
chunks.explain: It is better for her not to ask.

mishnayos.summary: A man who sold himself and his children to a non-Jew is not redeemed, but his children are. A field sold to a non-Jew still needs bikkurim when a Jew buys it back.

chunks.he: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו לְגוֹי,
chunks.en: Someone who sells himself and his children to a non-Jew,
chunks.st: With regard to one who sells himself and his children as slaves to gentiles,

chunks.en: we do not redeem him,
chunks.st: he is not redeemed,

chunks.en: but we do redeem the children
chunks.st: but the children are redeemed

chunks.en: after their father dies.
chunks.st: after their father’s death,
chunks.stMore: as there is no reason to penalize them.

chunks.en: Someone who sells his field to a non-Jew, and then
chunks.st: One who sells his field to a gentile

chunks.en: a Jew bought it back from him,
chunks.st: must purchase
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz reads it as the seller buying it back; these words follow our Hebrew text.

chunks.en: the buyer brings bikkurim from it,
chunks.st: and bring the first fruits from the field that he sold,

words.note: The first fruits, brought to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: for the betterment of the world.

mishnayos.summary: When someone must pay from his land, the mishnah tells which kind of land is used: the best, the middle, or the poorest.

chunks.en: For damages, they judge the value using the best land,
chunks.st: The court appraises land of superior quality [iddit] for payment to injured parties.

chunks.en: and a lender collects from the middle land,
chunks.st: And a creditor collects his debt from the debtor’s intermediate-quality land.

chunks.en: and a woman's kesubah from the poorest land.
chunks.st: And payment of a woman’s marriage contract is collected from her husband’s inferior-quality land.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: a woman's kesubah also comes from the middle land.
chunks.st: Payment of a woman’s marriage contract is also collected from intermediate-quality land.

mishnayos.summary: A debt is not taken from land the borrower already sold to others while he still has land of his own. From orphans, it is taken only from the poorest land.

chunks.en: We do not collect from property that was sold to others when
chunks.st: Payment of a debt or other obligation is not collected from liened property that has been sold to a third party when

words.note: Land that was sold, but still tied to a debt.

chunks.en: there is property that is still free,
chunks.st: the debtor still has unsold property,

words.note: Not sold to anyone.

chunks.en: even if it is the poorest land.
chunks.st: even when this unsold property is inferior-quality land.
chunks.stMore: The creditor cannot collect his debt from liened property that the debtor has sold to another person as long as the debtor is still in possession of other property, even if the remaining assets are inferior to those to which the creditor would otherwise have been entitled.

chunks.en: We do not collect from the property of orphans,
chunks.st: If one who owed money died and his children inherited his property, the father’s debt can be collected from the property of the orphans

chunks.en: except from the poorest land.
chunks.st: only from inferior-quality land.

mishnayos.summary: To help the world, some payments may not be taken from land that was already sold to others. Also, a person who returns a lost object does not have to swear.

chunks.he: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין לַאֲכִילַת פֵּרוֹת וּלְשֶׁבַח קַרְקָעוֹת
chunks.en: We do not take from sold property for eaten fruit or for land that got better,
chunks.st: The court does not appropriate liened property that has been sold to a third party for the consumption of produce or for the enhanced value of land.
chunks.stMore: If one appropriated a field and sold it, and the buyer worked the land, enhanced it, and grew produce on it, and then the initial owner from whom the field had been stolen took back the land and the produce from the buyer, compensating him only for his expenses, then the buyer may go back to the seller, i.e., the robber, and collect his losses. He can collect the purchase price of the field even from property that the robber sold to another person. By contrast, the value of the produce and the enhancement in the value of the field, which resulted from his actions, may be collected only from the robber’s unsold property.

chunks.en: or for feeding a man's wife and daughters, from sold property,
chunks.st: And similarly, payment for the sustenance of a man’s wife and daughters cannot be collected from his liened property.
chunks.stMore: One of the stipulations included in a marriage contract is that after the husband dies, his widow and daughters are entitled to sustenance from his estate. This sustenance cannot be collected from husband’s liened property that has been sold to another person, but only from his unsold property inherited by his heirs.

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: All of these enactments were made for the betterment of the world.

chunks.en: And someone who finds a lost object
chunks.st: And it was further instituted that one who finds a lost item and returns it to its rightful owner is

chunks.en: does not have to swear,
chunks.st: not required to take an oath that he did not keep any part of the lost item for himself.

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: This ordinance was also instituted for the betterment of the world.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches about a guardian who takes care of orphans, and about people who ruin someone else's food or a korban on purpose or by mistake.

chunks.en: Orphans who are taken care of by a homeowner,
chunks.st: With regard to orphans who are living with a homeowner
chunks.stMore: who takes care of all their needs and affairs, even if neither their father nor the court officially appointed him to this task,

chunks.en: or whose father chose a guardian for them,
chunks.st: or if their father appointed a steward [apotropos] for them,

chunks.en: he must take maaser from their fruit.
chunks.st: this person is obligated to tithe their produce.

chunks.en: A guardian whom the orphans' father chose
chunks.st: With regard to a steward who was appointed by the orphans’ father,

chunks.en: must swear. If the beis din chose him,
chunks.st: when he returns all of the property to the orphans upon their reaching adulthood, he takes an oath that he took nothing of theirs for himself. By contrast, if the court appointed him

chunks.en: he does not have to swear.
chunks.st: to serve as a steward for them, then he is not required to take such an oath.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says,
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:

chunks.en: it is the other way around.
chunks.st: The matters are reversed.
chunks.stMore: A steward appointed by the court takes an oath, but a steward appointed by the orphans’ father is not required to do so.

chunks.en: Someone who makes food tamei, or mixes terumah into it, or pours wine for avodah zarah, by mistake,
chunks.st: With regard to one who renders another’s food ritually impure, or one who mixes teruma with another’s non-sacred produce, or one who pours another’s wine as a libation before an idol, in each of these cases causing the other a monetary loss, if he acted unintentionally,

words.en: and one who mixes in terumah
and one who pours for avodah zarah

chunks.en: does not have to pay. On purpose,
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying for the damage. If he acted intentionally,

chunks.he: חַיָּב. הַכֹּהֲנִים שֶׁפִּגְּלוּ בַמִּקְדָּשׁ מְזִידִין, חַיָּבִין:
chunks.en: he must pay. Kohanim who spoil a korban in the Beis HaMikdash on purpose must pay.
chunks.explain: They ruined it by thinking wrong thoughts while bringing it.
chunks.st: he is liable to pay. If priests disqualified an offering with improper intention in the Temple, by expressing, while sacrificing the offering, the intention of sprinkling the blood of the offering, burning its fats on the altar, or consuming it, after its appointed time, and they did so intentionally, they are liable
chunks.stMore: to pay the value of the offering to its owner, who must now bring another offering.

words.note: A korban ruined by wrong thoughts about when it will be eaten.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda told the Sages four halachos he had received, including two rules made to help people do teshuvah and to help the mizbeach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda testified
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda testified before the Sages

chunks.en: about a girl who cannot hear whose father married her off,
chunks.st: about the case of a deaf-mute woman who was married off by her father
chunks.stMore: when she was a minor, so that her marriage took effect by Torah law.

chunks.en: that she can leave the marriage with a get.
chunks.st: He said that she can be released from her marriage through a bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: whether as a minor or after she reaches adulthood. Although as a deaf-mute woman she is not legally competent to give her consent, the divorce is effective because divorce does not require the woman’s consent.

chunks.he: וְעַל קְטַנָּה בַת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְכֹהֵן,
chunks.en: And about a young daughter of a Yisrael who married a Kohen,
chunks.st: And similarly, he testified about the case of the minor daughter of a non-priest who was orphaned from her father and then married off to a priest
chunks.stMore: by her mother or brother, so that her marriage took effect by rabbinic law.

chunks.en: that she may eat terumah,
chunks.st: He said that nevertheless she may partake of teruma,
chunks.stMore: although by Torah law it is prohibited for one who is not in a priestly household to partake of teruma.

chunks.en: and if she dies,
chunks.st: And furthermore if this girl dies,

chunks.en: her husband inherits from her.
chunks.st: then her husband inherits her estate.
chunks.stMore: It is not said that because the validity of the marriage is by rabbinic law and not Torah law he is not entitled to inherit from her.

chunks.en: And about a stolen beam that was built into a big building,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda further testified about a stolen beam that was already built into a large building [bira],

chunks.en: that the owner gets only its value,
chunks.st: that the victim of the robbery receives only the value of the beam but not the beam itself,

chunks.en: to help people who do teshuvah.
chunks.explain: The thief does not have to break the building to return it.
chunks.st: due to an ordinance instituted for the penitent.
chunks.stMore: By Torah law, a robber is obligated to return any stolen item in his possession, provided that its form has not been altered. If one stole a beam and incorporated it into a building, then by Torah law he would have to destroy the building and return the beam. In order to encourage repentance, the Sages were lenient and allowed a robber to return the value of the beam.

chunks.he: וְעַל חַטָּאת הַגְּזוּלָה שֶׁלֹּא נוֹדְעָה לָרַבִּים,

chunks.stMore: i.e., to foster peace and prevent strife and controversy:

chunks.en: A poor man who knocks olives off the top of an olive tree:

Bundles that were forgotten in the field.
The corner of the field left for the poor.

mishnayos.summary: A woman may lend tools to a neighbor who may not be careful with mitzvos, but she may not help her do the aveirah. All this is to keep peace.

chunks.he: מַשְׁאֶלֶת אִשָּׁה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ הַחֲשׁוּדָה עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית,
chunks.en: A woman may lend to her friend who is suspected about Shemitah fruit,
chunks.st: A woman may lend utensils to her friend who is suspect with regard to eating produce that grew in the Sabbatical Year after the time that such produce must be removed from the house and may no longer be eaten.
chunks.stMore: The utensils that she may lend her include:

words.note: The seventh year, when fields rest.

chunks.en: a sifter, a sieve, a millstone, and an oven,
chunks.st: A winnow, a sieve, a mill, and an oven.
chunks.stMore: Lending her such utensils is not considered aiding in the commission of a transgression.

chunks.he: אֲבָל לֹא תָבֹר וְלֹא תִטְחַן עִמָּהּ.
chunks.en: but she may not sort or grind with her.
chunks.st: But she may not select the grain from the chaff or grind wheat with her,
chunks.stMore: i.e., she may not actively assist her in the performance of a sin.

chunks.he: אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר מַשְׁאֶלֶת לְאֵשֶׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: The wife of a chaver may lend to the wife of an am ha'aretz

words.note: A person very careful with tumah, terumah and maaser.
An am ha'aretz is someone not careful with these mitzvos.

chunks.en: a sifter and a sieve,
chunks.st: a winnow and a sieve,

chunks.en: and she may sort, grind, and sift with her,
chunks.st: and she may even select, grind, and sift with her.

chunks.en: but once she pours the water in,
chunks.st: But once the wife of the am ha’aretz pours water into the flour,

chunks.en: she may not touch it with her,
chunks.st: the wife of the ḥaver may not touch anything with her,

chunks.he: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַחֲזִיקִין יְדֵי עוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵרָה.
chunks.en: because we may not help people who do aveiros.

chunks.st: And one may assist gentiles who work the land during the Sabbatical Year,

mishnayos.summary: A husband may cancel a messenger who brings the get for him. But once the wife's own messenger receives the get for her, the husband can no longer take it back.

chunks.en: Someone who says, "Receive this get for my wife,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who says to another: Receive this bill of divorce for my wife,

chunks.en: or "Take this get to my wife,"
chunks.st: or: Deliver this bill of divorce to my wife as my agent,

chunks.en: if he wants to take it back,
chunks.st: if the husband seeks to retract his designation and cancel the agency,

chunks.en: he may take it back. A woman who said,
chunks.st: he can retract it until the document reaches his wife’s possession. However, in the case of a woman who said to an agent:

chunks.en: "Receive my get for me,"
chunks.st: Receive my bill of divorce for me,

chunks.en: if the husband wants to take it back,
chunks.st: and the husband handed the bill of divorce to her agent, if the husband seeks to retract his decision to divorce his wife upon receipt of the bill of divorce by the agent,

chunks.en: he may not take it back.
chunks.st: he cannot retract it.
chunks.stMore: Once the bill of divorce is transferred to her agent, its legal status is like that of a bill of divorce that was handed directly to her, and the divorce takes effect immediately.

chunks.en: So, if the husband said to him,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the husband said to the agent whom the woman designated to receive the bill of divorce:

chunks.en: "I do not want you to receive it for her,
chunks.st: I do not want [ee ifshi] for you to receive the bill of divorce for her;

chunks.en: but take it and give it to her,"
chunks.st: rather, deliver it and give it to her,

chunks.en: if he wants to take it back,
chunks.st: then if the husband seeks to retract his designation and cancel the agency,

chunks.he: יַחֲזֹר. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: he may take it back. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: he can retract it until it reaches his wife’s possession. Since the husband does not agree to have the divorce take effect upon receipt by his wife’s agent, he changes the designation of the agent and designates him as his own agent for delivery. Therefore, the divorce takes effect only when the bill of divorce reaches his wife’s possession. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: even if she says, "Take my get for me,"
chunks.st: Even a woman who did not instruct the agent: Receive my bill of divorce for me but says: Take my bill of divorce for me,
chunks.stMore: thereby designates the agent as an agent of receipt on her behalf. Therefore,

chunks.en: if he wants to take it back,
chunks.st: if after handing the bill of divorce to the agent the husband seeks to retract his decision and cancel the agency,

chunks.en: he may not take it back.
chunks.st: he cannot retract it.

mishnayos.summary: When a woman's messenger receives her get, two pairs of witnesses must tell what happened. The mishnah also teaches who may receive the get of a young girl.

chunks.en: A woman who said,
chunks.st: A woman who said to an agent:

chunks.en: "Receive my get for me,"
chunks.st: Receive my bill of divorce for me,

chunks.en: needs two groups of witnesses:
chunks.st: requires two sets of witnesses
chunks.stMore: to confirm that she was divorced when the agent received the bill of divorce. She requires

chunks.en: two who say, "She said it in front of us," and two
chunks.st: two witnesses who say: In our presence she said to the agent: Receive my bill of divorce on my behalf, and two

chunks.en: who say, "In front of us he received it and tore it."
chunks.explain: Tearing the get shows it was used.
chunks.st: who say: In our presence the agent received the bill of divorce and tore it.

chunks.en: Even if the same people are the first ones and the last ones,
chunks.st: This testimony is effective even if two people are the first pair of witnesses and the same two are the latter pair of witnesses,

chunks.en: or one from the first and one
chunks.st: or if there is one witness from the first pair of witnesses and one witness

chunks.en: from the last, and one more joins with them.
chunks.st: from the latter pair, and one additional witness joins with them as the second witness in both testimonies.

chunks.en: A young girl who is engaged:
chunks.st: With regard to a betrothed young woman,

chunks.en: she or her father may receive her get.
chunks.st: she and her father are each eligible to receive her bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: and the divorce takes effect at the moment that either of them receives the bill of divorce.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: two hands cannot take for one person together,
chunks.st: Two hands do not have the right to acquire an item on behalf of one person as one.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אָבִיהָ מְקַבֵּל אֶת גִּטָּהּ בִּלְבָד.
chunks.en: rather only her father receives her get.
chunks.st: Rather, her father alone receives her bill of divorce on her behalf.
chunks.stMore: And there is another principle:

chunks.he: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לִשְׁמֹר אֶת גִּטָּהּ,
chunks.en: And any girl who cannot guard her get
chunks.st: Any female who is unable to safeguard her bill of divorce

chunks.en: cannot be divorced.
chunks.st: is unable to be divorced.

mishnayos.summary: A young girl cannot make a messenger, but her father can. The mishnah also teaches what happens when a messenger gives or receives the get in a different place than he was told.

chunks.en: A young girl who said, "Receive my get for me,"
chunks.st: In the case of a minor girl who said to an agent: Receive my bill of divorce for me,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ גֵט עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ גֵּט לְיָדָהּ.
chunks.en: it is not a get until it reaches her hand.
chunks.st: it is not a valid bill of divorce until the bill of divorce reaches her possession.

chunks.en: So if the husband wants to take it back,
chunks.st: Therefore, if the husband seeks to retract his decision before his wife receives the bill of divorce,

chunks.en: he may take it back, because a child cannot make a messenger.
chunks.st: he can retract it, as a minor does not designate an agent.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, the agent is not an agent for receipt, and the divorce does not take effect when the husband hands the document to the agent. The agent is an agent for delivery, and the divorce takes effect when the bill of divorce enters the wife’s possession.

chunks.en: But if her father said to him,
chunks.st: And if her father said to the agent:

chunks.en: "Go and receive my daughter's get for her,"
chunks.st: Go out and receive my daughter’s bill of divorce on her behalf, then

chunks.en: if the husband wants to take it back,
chunks.st: if the husband seeks to retract his decision,

chunks.en: he may not take it back.
chunks.st: he cannot retract it.
chunks.stMore: As a father can receive the bill of divorce on behalf of his minor daughter, he can designate an agent for receipt, and the divorce takes effect when the husband hands the document to the agent.

chunks.en: Someone who says, "Give this get
chunks.st: With regard to one who says to an agent: Give this bill of divorce

chunks.en: to my wife in such-and-such a place,"
chunks.st: to my wife in such and such a place,

chunks.en: and he gave it to her in another place,
chunks.st: if the agent deviated and gave it to her in another place

chunks.en: it is not valid. But "She is in such-and-such a place,"
chunks.st: the divorce is invalid. However, if he said to the agent: Give this bill of divorce to my wife, she is in such and such a place,
chunks.stMore: without explicitly instructing the agent to give her the document there,

chunks.en: and he gave it to her in another place,
chunks.st: and he gave it to her in another place

chunks.en: it is valid. A woman who said, "Receive for me
chunks.st: the divorce is valid. With regard to the woman who when designating her agent for receipt said to her agent: Receive

chunks.en: my get in such-and-such a place,"
chunks.st: my bill of divorce for me in such and such a place,

chunks.en: and he received it for her in another place,
chunks.st: and he received it for her in another place,

chunks.en: "Bring me my get from such-and-such a place,"
chunks.st: If she said to him: Bring me my bill of divorce from such and such a place,

chunks.en: and he brought it to her from another place, it is valid.
chunks.st: and he brought it for her from another place, it is valid.

chunks.st: An Israelite woman married to a priest partakes of teruma. If she says to an agent: Bring me my bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: designating him as an agent for delivery,

chunks.en: or "Divorce her," or "Write a letter and give it to her,"
chunks.st: or: Divorce her, or: Write a letter and give it to her,

chunks.en: they should write it and give it.
chunks.st: they should write the document and give it to her.

chunks.en: "Treat her by the law,"
chunks.st: or: Treat her according to the law [nimus],

chunks.en: "Treat her properly,"
chunks.st: or: Treat her appropriately,

chunks.en: did not say anything.

chunks.st: At first the Sages would say:

only to make the world better.

mishnayos.summary: When two gittin get mixed up, both must be given to each wife. When several gittin are written on one page, the witnesses' signatures decide which ones are valid.

chunks.he: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁשָּׁלְחוּ שְׁנֵי גִטִּין שָׁוִין וְנִתְעָרְבוּ,
chunks.en: Two men who sent two gittin that were the same, and they got mixed up,
chunks.st: With regard to a case of two men who sent their wives two identical bills of divorce with an agent, as both their names and their wives’ names are identical, and the two bills of divorce were mixed up,

chunks.en: he gives both to this wife and both to that wife.
chunks.st: the agent should hand both bills of divorce to this wife and both of them to that wife, so that each wife definitely receives her bill of divorce, although it is unclear which one is hers.

chunks.en: So, if one of them got lost,
chunks.st: Therefore, if one of the bills of divorce was lost before it was given to both women,

chunks.en: the other one is cancelled.
chunks.st: the other is void,
chunks.stMore: because it is unknown which bill of divorce was meant for which woman.

chunks.en: Five men who wrote one shared text in the get,
chunks.st: With regard to five husbands who wrote a general wording in the bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: i.e., who wrote one common bill of divorce for their wives with a single formula, writing that

chunks.he: אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי מְגָרֵשׁ פְּלוֹנִית וּפְלוֹנִי פְּלוֹנִית,
chunks.en: "The man so-and-so divorces so-and-so, and so-and-so divorces so-and-so,"
chunks.st: so-and-so divorces his wife so-and-so, and so-and-so divorces so-and-so,

chunks.en: and the witnesses are below,
chunks.st: and the witnesses signed below,

chunks.en: all of them are valid,
chunks.st: in this case all of these bills of divorce that were combined into one bill are valid;

chunks.en: and it must be given to each one.
chunks.st: and the bill must be handed to each and every wife individually, so they will all be divorced by it.

chunks.he: הָיָה כָתוּב טֹפֶס לְכָל אַחַת וְאַחַת,
chunks.en: If a separate form was written for each one,
chunks.st: If the scribe was writing a separate formula in the bill of divorce for each and every couple,

chunks.en: and the witnesses are below,
chunks.st: and the witnesses signed below,

chunks.en: the one the witnesses are read with is valid.
chunks.st: the formula with which the witnesses’ signatures are read is valid. In other words, the formula directly underneath which they signed is valid, and the others are not valid.

mishnayos.summary: When two gittin are written side by side and the witnesses sign across both, the way they signed decides which get is valid.

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי גִטִּין שֶׁכְּתָבָן זֶה בְצַד זֶה
chunks.en: Two gittin written one next to the other,
chunks.st: With regard to two bills of divorce that a scribe wrote on the same paper one next to the other,

chunks.he: וּשְׁנַיִם עֵדִים עִבְרִים בָּאִים מִתַּחַת זֶה
chunks.en: and two Hebrew witnesses go from under this one
chunks.st: and the signatures of two Hebrew witnesses, i.e., witnesses who signed in Hebrew from right to left, extend from underneath this bill of divorce on the right

chunks.he: לְתַחַת זֶה וּשְׁנַיִם עֵדִים יְוָנִים בָּאִים
chunks.en: to under that one, and two Greek witnesses go
chunks.st: to underneath that bill of divorce on the left, and the signatures of two Greek witnesses, i.e., who signed in Greek from left to right, extend

chunks.en: from under that one to under this one,
chunks.st: from underneath that bill of divorce on the left to underneath this bill of divorce on the right,

chunks.en: the get that the first witnesses are read with
chunks.st: the bill of divorce with which the names of the first two witnesses are read [nikra’in]

chunks.he: כָּשֵׁר. עֵד אֶחָד עִבְרִי וְעֵד אֶחָד יְוָנִי,
chunks.en: is valid. If one Hebrew witness and one Greek witness,
chunks.st: is valid. The other bill of divorce is invalid, as it is not considered signed by these witnesses. If one witness signed in Hebrew from right to left, and one witness signed beneath him in Greek from left to right, and

chunks.he: עֵד אֶחָד עִבְרִי וְעֵד אֶחָד יְוָנִי
chunks.en: one Hebrew witness and one Greek witness,
chunks.st: underneath that signature one witness signed in Hebrew, and beneath him one witness signed in Greek,

chunks.en: go from under this one to under that one,
chunks.st: with the signatures extending from underneath this bill of divorce to underneath that bill of divorce,

chunks.en: both are not valid.
chunks.st: both bills of divorce are invalid.

mishnayos.summary: Where the witnesses sign on the page matters. The mishnah gives cases of gittin written in different directions and tells which are valid.

chunks.he: שִׁיֵּר מִקְצַת הַגֵּט וּכְתָבוֹ בַדַּף הַשֵּׁנִי,
chunks.en: If he left out part of the get and wrote it on the next column,
chunks.st: If a scribe left out part of the bill of divorce and wrote it in the second column,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the bill of divorce is written in two columns on one paper,

chunks.en: and the witnesses are below,
chunks.st: and the signatures of the witnesses are beneath the second column,

chunks.en: it is valid. If witnesses signed at the top of the page,
chunks.st: it is a valid bill of divorce. If the witnesses signed at the top of the column,

chunks.en: on the side,
chunks.st: on the side,

chunks.en: or on the back of a plain get,
chunks.st: or on the back of an ordinary, non-folded bill of divorce,

chunks.en: it is not valid. If he put the top of this one
chunks.st: it is invalid. If the scribe placed the top of this bill of divorce

chunks.en: next to the top of that one,
chunks.st: next to the top of that bill of divorce
chunks.stMore: so that both are written in the same column but with the text in opposite directions,

chunks.en: and the witnesses are in the middle,
chunks.st: and the witnesses signed in the middle, between the bills of divorce,

chunks.en: both are not valid.
chunks.st: both bills of divorce are invalid.

chunks.en: If the end of this one is next to
chunks.st: If he placed the end of this bill of divorce next to

chunks.en: the end of that one,
chunks.st: the end of that bill of divorce,

chunks.en: and the witnesses are in the middle,
chunks.st: and the witnesses signed in the middle between them,

chunks.en: the one the witnesses are read with
chunks.st: the bill of divorce with which the witnesses’ signatures are read,

chunks.en: is valid. If the top of this one is next to
chunks.st: i.e., the bill that is written in the same direction as the signatures, is valid. If he placed the top of this bill of divorce next to

chunks.en: the end of that one,
chunks.st: the end of that bill of divorce,

chunks.en: and the witnesses are in the middle,
chunks.st: and the witnesses signed in the middle,

chunks.en: the one at whose end the witnesses are read is valid.
chunks.st: the bill of divorce at the end of which the witnesses are read, i.e., the upper bill of divorce, is valid.

mishnayos.summary: A get is valid even if written in one language and signed in another, and even if the witnesses sign in different ways. A get the husband was forced to give is valid only if a Jewish beis din made him.

chunks.en: A get written in Hebrew with its witnesses in Greek,
chunks.st: With regard to a bill of divorce that was written in Hebrew and its witnesses signed in Greek,

chunks.en: or in Greek with its witnesses in Hebrew,
chunks.st: or that was written in Greek and its witnesses signed in Hebrew,

chunks.he: עֵד אֶחָד עִבְרִי וְעֵד אֶחָד יְוָנִי,
chunks.en: or one Hebrew witness and one Greek witness,
chunks.st: or in which one witness signed in Hebrew and one witness signed in Greek,

chunks.en: or the scribe wrote it and one witness signed,
chunks.st: or if a bill of divorce has the writing of a scribe, and the scribe identifies his handwriting, and one witness verifies his signature,

chunks.en: it is valid. "So-and-so, witness,"
chunks.st: it is valid as though two witnesses testified to ratify their signatures. As for the wording of the signature, if a witness signed: So-and-so, witness,
chunks.stMore: without mentioning his father’s name,

chunks.en: it is valid. "The son of so-and-so, witness,"
chunks.st: it is valid. Similarly, if he did not write his name and instead wrote: Son of so-and-so, witness,

chunks.he: כָּשֵׁר. אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי בֶּן אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי,
chunks.en: it is valid. "So-and-so son of so-and-so,"
chunks.st: it is valid. If he wrote: So-and-so, son of so-and-so,

chunks.en: and he did not write "witness,"
chunks.st: but did not write the word witness,

chunks.he: כָּשֵׁר. וְכָךְ הָיוּ נְקִיֵּי הַדַּעַת שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם עוֹשִׂין.
chunks.en: it is valid. And this is what the careful people of Yerushalayim used to do.
chunks.st: it is valid. And this is what the scrupulous people of Jerusalem would do,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they would sign without the word witness.

chunks.en: If he wrote his nickname and her nickname,
chunks.st: As for the names of the husband and wife, if the scribe wrote his surname [ḥanikhato] or nickname and her surname or nickname,

chunks.en: it is valid. A get that he was forced to give:
chunks.st: it is valid. With regard to a bill of divorce that the husband was compelled by the court to write and give his wife,

chunks.en: by Jews, it is valid,
chunks.st: if he was compelled by a Jewish court it is valid,

chunks.en: but by non-Jews, it is not valid.
chunks.st: but if he was compelled by gentiles it is invalid.

chunks.he: וּבְגוֹיִם, חוֹבְטִין אוֹתוֹ וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ עֲשֵׂה
chunks.en: But non-Jews may hit him and say to him, "Do
chunks.st: But with regard to gentiles they may beat him at the request of the Jewish court and say to him: Do

chunks.en: what the Jews tell you," and it is valid.
chunks.st: what the Jews are telling you, and it is a valid divorce.

mishnayos.summary: If everyone in town says a woman is engaged or divorced, we believe it, unless there is another way to explain the talk.

chunks.en: If word went around the city that she is engaged,
chunks.st: If a rumor circulated in the city that an unmarried woman is betrothed,

chunks.en: she is engaged.
chunks.st: she is considered to be betrothed.

chunks.en: Divorced, she is divorced,
chunks.st: Similarly, if a rumor circulated that a married woman is divorced, she is divorced,

chunks.en: as long as there is no other explanation.
chunks.st: provided there is no valid alternative explanation [amatla] for the rumor.

chunks.en: What is an explanation?
chunks.st: What is considered a valid explanation?

chunks.en: "So-and-so divorced
chunks.st: For example, it is a case where there is a rumor that so-and-so divorced

chunks.en: his wife with a condition,"
chunks.st: his wife but that the bill of divorce was given to her conditionally.
chunks.stMore: It is therefore possible that the condition was not fulfilled and she is not actually divorced.

chunks.en: "he threw her kiddushin to her,
chunks.st: Similarly, if there is a rumor that a woman was betrothed but that the man threw her betrothal, i.e., the money or document of betrothal, to her,

chunks.he: סָפֵק קָרוֹב לָהּ סָפֵק קָרוֹב לוֹ,
chunks.en: maybe closer to her, maybe closer to him,"
chunks.st: and it is uncertain whether it was closer to her and uncertain whether it was closer to him,
chunks.stMore: and therefore the status of their betrothal is likewise uncertain,

chunks.en: this is an explanation.
chunks.st: this is considered a valid explanation.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai, Beis Hillel, and Rabbi Akiva argue about what reasons let a man divorce his wife, and each learns it from a pasuk.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,

chunks.he: לֹא יְגָרֵשׁ אָדָם אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ אֶלָּא
chunks.en: a man should not divorce his wife unless

chunks.he: אִם כֵּן מָצָא בָהּ דְּבַר עֶרְוָה,
chunks.en: he found in her something not modest,
as it says in Devarim,
"Because he found in her something not proper."
And Beis Hillel say,
even if she burned his food,
as it says there,
"Because he found in her something not proper."
Rabbi Akiva says,
even if he found another woman nicer looking than her,
as it says there,

chunks.he: וְהָיָה אִם לֹא תִמְצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו:
chunks.en: "And if she does not find favor in his eyes."
